title: PTE Academic Format: The One-Glance Overview
summary: The 3-part, ~2-hour, AI-scored structure of PTE Academic — and why 'integrated skills' is the whole game.

nodes.label: Speaking & Writing
nodes.note: ~76–84 min · Read Aloud, Describe Image, essay & more

nodes.label: Listening
nodes.note: Summarize Spoken Text, Write from Dictation & more

nodes.label: Integrated skills
nodes.note: One task can score two skills at once

chunks.heading: Three parts, about two hours
chunks.body: PTE Academic runs in **three parts** in a fixed order: **Speaking & Writing** (about 76–84 minutes), then **Reading**, then **Listening**. In total you'll answer **65–75 questions** drawn from about **22 question types**, all on a computer at a test centre.
chunks.realExample: You sit down, put on the headset, and the first thing you do is a short spoken 'Personal Introduction' that isn't even scored — then straight into Read Aloud. No long reading passages to warm up on.
chunks.memoryHook: Order never changes: Speak+Write → Read → Listen. S-W-R-L.

chunks.heading: It's scored by AI, 10–90
chunks.body: Your responses are marked by **Pearson's AI scoring**, with some responses also reviewed by a human, on the **10–90 Global Scale of English (GSE)**. Machine scoring means **consistency and speed** — results usually come within a couple of days — but also that **clarity and timing matter more than clever, risky answers**.
chunks.realExample: In Read Aloud, a steady, clearly-pronounced read scores better than a fast, dramatic one — the AI rewards fluency and intelligibility, not performance.
chunks.memoryHook: A machine is listening. Be clear, steady and on-time — not fancy.

chunks.heading: Integrated skills — one task, two scores
chunks.body: PTE's defining feature: many tasks are **integrated**, so a single task feeds **more than one skill score**. Read Aloud counts for **speaking and reading**; Write from Dictation counts for **listening and writing**; Summarize Written Text counts for **reading and writing**.
chunks.realExample: Nail 'Write from Dictation' (just type the sentence you hear, exactly) and you quietly boost BOTH your Listening and your Writing score from one 15-second task. High value for low effort.
chunks.memoryHook: Some tasks pay double. Hunt the two-skill tasks — they're the best ROI.

chunks.heading: What this means for your prep
chunks.body: Because scoring is integrated and automated, **prioritise the high-value repeatable tasks** (Read Aloud, Repeat Sentence, Write from Dictation) and practise **timing and clarity** over memorised templates. Every task has a strict on-screen timer.
chunks.realExample: A candidate weak in Writing lifted their Writing score mainly by drilling Write from Dictation and Summarize Written Text — Listening and Reading tasks that also feed Writing.
chunks.memoryHook: Train the double-scoring tasks first. They lift two bars at once.

recall.q: What are the three parts of PTE Academic, in order?
recall.a: Speaking & Writing, then Reading, then Listening.

recall.q: How is PTE Academic scored, and on what scale?
recall.a: By Pearson's AI (with some human review) on the 10–90 Global Scale of English.

recall.q: What does 'integrated skills' mean in PTE?
recall.a: A single task can contribute to more than one skill score — e.g. Read Aloud scores speaking and reading.

recall.q: Which task boosts both Listening and Writing at once?
recall.a: Write from Dictation — you type the sentence you hear, and it feeds both scores.

recall.q: Roughly how long is the test and how many questions?
recall.a: About two hours, with 65–75 questions across roughly 22 question types.
